Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 1:

Surat al-Isra' [Meccan, except verses 26, 32, and 57 from verse 73 to the end of verse 80, which are Medinan; its verses number 111; it was revealed after Surat al-Qasas]

﴿Glory be to Him﴾, i.e., exalted above any imperfection, ﴿who took His servant﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿by night﴾ — it is in the accusative of time (nasb 'ala al-zarf), and al-isra' means travelling by night. The benefit of its indefinite form is to indicate the shortness of its duration, ﴿from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque﴾, which is Bayt al-Maqdis, so called because of its distance [from Mecca], ﴿whose surroundings We have blessed﴾ with fruits and rivers, ﴿so that We might show him some of Our signs﴾, the wonders of Our power. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, i.e., the One who knows the sayings and deeds of the Prophet (ﷺ). Thus He bestowed upon him the Night Journey, which included his meeting with the prophets, his ascent to the heavens, his seeing the wonders of the malakut (the unseen realm), and his intimate conversation with Him, the Exalted. For the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"I was brought the Buraq, a white animal, larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, which places its hoof at the furthest point of its sight. I mounted it and it carried me until I came to Bayt al-Maqdis. I tied the animal to the ring to which the prophets tie their animals, then I entered and prayed two rak'ahs in it. Then I went out, and Jibril came to me with a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, and I chose the milk. Jibril said: 'You have chosen the fitrah.' Then I was taken up to the lowest heaven, and Jibril asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and behold, there was Adam, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then I was taken up to the second heaven, and Jibril asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and behold, there were the two cousins, Yahya and Isa, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then we were taken up to the third heaven, and Jibril asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and behold, there was Yusuf, and he had been given half of beauty. He welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then we were taken up to the fourth heaven, and Jibril asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and behold, there was Idris, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then we were taken up to the fifth heaven, and Jibril asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and behold, there was Harun, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then we were taken up to the sixth heaven, and Jibril asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and behold, there was Musa, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then we were taken up to the seventh heaven, and Jibril asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and behold, there was Ibrahim, leaning against the Bayt al-Ma'mur, which seventy thousand angels enter every day, and they never return to it. Then he went to Sidrat al-Muntaha, whose leaves were like the ears of elephants and whose fruit was like large jars. When there covered it what covered it by the command of Allah, it changed, and no one of Allah's creation is able to describe its beauty. He said: Then Allah revealed to me what He revealed and enjoined upon me fifty prayers every day and night. I descended until I came to Musa, who said: 'What has your Lord enjoined upon your nation?' I said: 'Fifty prayers every day and night.' He said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it for your nation, for your nation cannot bear that, and I have tested the Children of Israel and known them.' So I returned to my Lord and said: 'O Lord, lighten it for my nation,' and He removed five from me. I returned to Musa, who said: 'What have you done?' I said: 'He has removed five from me.' He said: 'Your nation cannot bear that. Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it for your nation.' So I kept returning between my Lord and Musa, and He kept removing five, five, until He said: 'O Muhammad, they are five prayers every day and night, and each prayer is worth ten, so those are fifty prayers. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him; if he does it, ten are recorded for him. Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, nothing is recorded for him; if he does it, one evil deed is recorded for him.' So I descended until I came to Musa and informed him, and he said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it, for your nation cannot bear that.' I said: 'I have returned to my Lord until I felt shy.'" Narrated by al-Shaykhan, and the wording is that of Muslim. Al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic."

﴿And We gave Musa the Book﴾, the Tawrat (Torah), ﴿that﴾ [the particle ʾan] ﴿do not take besides Me a trustee﴾, those to whom they entrust their affairs. In another reading, ﴿tattakhidhu﴾ is read with the second person, ta, as a shift (iltifat) (a change in grammatical person). In that case ﴿an﴾ is an extra particle (za'ida), and the word "saying" (al-qawl) is implied (mudmar).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 3:

﴿Descendants of those whom We carried with Noah﴾ in the ship ﴿grateful servant﴾ abundantly thankful to Us, praising Us in all his circumstances.

"And We decreed" — i.e., We revealed ﴿in the Book﴾, the Torah, ﴿that you would surely cause corruption in the land﴾ — the land of al-Sham (Syria) — through acts of disobedience ﴿and you would surely become haughty with great haughtiness﴾ — you would commit great transgression.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 5:

﴿When the promise of the first of the two came,﴾ the first of the two corruptions. ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours of great might,﴾ possessors of strength in war and in violence. ﴿And they went through the houses,﴾ they roamed in search of you, ﴿and it was a promise fulfilled.﴾ ﴿and they went through the houses﴾ among your homes, to kill you and take you captive. ﴿And it was a promise fulfilled.﴾ They had already corrupted the first time by killing Zechariah, so He sent against them Goliath (Jalut) and his soldiers, who killed them, took their children captive, and destroyed the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 17, verse 6:

﴿Al-karrah﴾ (the turn of fortune, i.e., the dynasty and the victory) ﴿against them﴾ after a hundred years, by the killing of Jalut (Goliath); ﴿nafiran﴾ (a clan, i.e., a tribe).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 7:

﴿If you do good﴾ by obedience ﴿you do good for yourselves﴾, because its reward is for them. ﴿And if you do evil﴾ by corruption ﴿then it is for them﴾, their evil, ﴿and the promise of the last time﴾ (the second occasion) ﴿came﴾, We sent them ﴿to distress your faces﴾, to grieve you by killing and taking captives, a grief that appears on your faces, ﴿and to enter the Masjid﴾, Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and destroy it ﴿as they entered it the first time﴾ and destroyed it, ﴿and to destroy what they had overcome﴾, to conquer over it, ﴿with complete destruction﴾, annihilation. They corrupted a second time by killing Yahya, so God sent against them Bukhtunassar (Nebuchadnezzar), who killed thousands of them, took their offspring captive, and destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 8:

﴿Your Lord may have mercy upon you﴾ after the second time, ﴿if you repent﴾, ﴿but if you return﴾ to corruption, ﴿We shall return﴾ to punishment. They did return, by denying Muhammad (ﷺ), so he (ﷺ) was given power over them: the killing of Qurayzah, the expulsion of al-Nadir, and the imposition of the jizya (poll tax) upon them. ﴿A prison﴾: a confinement and a jail.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 9:

﴿For that which﴾ i.e., for the way which ﴿is most upright﴾, more just and more correct.

﴿And﴾ He informs that ﴿for those who do not believe in the Hereafter We have prepared﴾ (a'tadna, meaning a'dadna, "We have readied") ﴿for them a painful punishment﴾ (ʿadhāban alīman), meaning one that causes pain, which is the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 11:

﴿And man invokes evil⁠﴾ against himself and his family when he is vexed, ﴿his supplication⁠﴾, i.e., like his supplication for him ﴿for good⁠﴾. ﴿And man⁠﴾, meaning the species, ﴿was hasty⁠﴾ in supplicating against himself, and in not considering its outcome.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 12:

﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾ indicating Our power. ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night﴾ We obscured its light with darkness, ﴿so that you might rest therein﴾; and the idafa (genitive construction) here is for specification. ﴿Illuminating﴾, i.e., making things visible through its light (mubsiran, "illuminating," is an adjective of the sign, meaning the day's light makes things seen). ﴿That you may seek﴾ therein ﴿bounty from your Lord﴾ through earning. ﴿And that you may know﴾ by means of them ﴿the number of years and the reckoning﴾ for the times. ﴿And every thing﴾ that is needed ﴿We have detailed in detail﴾, i.e., We have made it clear with clarification.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 13:

﴿And every person We have fastened his omen to his neck﴾: his deed, which he carries ﴿around his neck﴾. It was singled out for mention because the attachment in it is stronger. And Mujahid said: "There is no child born except that on his neck is a paper, written upon it whether he is wretched or blessed." ﴿A book﴾: written, containing his deed, ﴿which he will find laid open﴾: two attributes of ﴿a book﴾.

﴿ḥasīban﴾ meaning: ﴿muḥāsaban﴾ (one who takes account)

Note on transliteration: the Arabic word ﴿حَسِيبًا﴾ is transliterated as ḥasīban, and ﴿مُحاسِبًا﴾ as muḥāsaban. Both are kept in Arabic script within the Qur'anic markers as required, with the English gloss given in parentheses.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 17, verse 15:

﴿Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his own self﴾, because the reward of his being guided belongs to him. ﴿And whoever goes astray only goes astray to its detriment﴾, because its sin falls upon it. ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾: no sinful soul shall bear the burden of another soul, i.e., shall not carry the sin of another soul. ﴿And We would never punish﴾ anyone ﴿until We have sent a messenger﴾ who makes clear to him what is obligatory upon him.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, a tafsir, or classical Qur'anic commentary) on Surah 17, verse 16:**

﴿مُتْرَفِيها﴾ (*mutrafīhā*) means their affluent ones, those made comfortable (*munaʿʿamīhā*), in the sense of their leaders, by obedience, through the tongue of Our messengers. ﴿فَفَسَقُوا فِيها﴾ (*fa-fasaqū fīhā*), meaning they went out from Our command. ﴿فَحَقَّ عَلَيْها القَوْل﴾ (*fa-ḥaqqa ʿalayhā al-qawl*), meaning the word was fulfilled against it, with the punishment. ﴿فَدَمَّرْناها تَدْمِيرًا﴾ (*fa-dammarnāhā tadmīrā*), meaning We destroyed it, by destroying its people and laying it to ruin.

﴿And how many﴾, meaning many, ﴿We destroyed of the generations﴾, meaning the nations, ﴿[as] All-Aware, All-Seeing﴾, meaning knowing their inward and outward states. The phrase ﴿bihi﴾ (by Him) is connected to ﴿bidhunubi﴾ (with the sins).

﴿Whoever desires﴾ by his deeds ﴿the immediate [life]﴾, i.e., the worldly life (al-dunya), ﴿We hasten for him﴾. The phrase al-ta'jīl lahu (the hastening for him) is a substitute (badal) for lahu, with the preposition (al-jarr) repeated. ﴿Then We make for him﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿Hell, which he will enter (yaslāhā), burning in it﴾, i.e., he will enter it, ﴿blamed (madhmūman)﴾, i.e., reproached, ﴿banished (madhūran)﴾, i.e., expelled from mercy.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 19:

﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the striving due to it﴾ does the deed appropriate to it, ﴿while he is a believer﴾ (a circumstantial clause, ḥāl), ﴿his striving will be appreciated﴾ with God, i.e., accepted and rewarded for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 20:

﴿Each﴾ of the two groups ﴿We extend﴾, that is, We give ﴿to these and to those﴾, a substitution (badal) ﴿from﴾, a phrase connected to ﴿We extend﴾, ﴿the gift of your Lord﴾ in this world, ﴿and the gift of your Lord was not﴾ in it ﴿restricted﴾, that is, withheld from anyone.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 21:

﴿Look how We have favored some of them over others﴾ in provision and standing, ﴿and the Hereafter is greater﴾ more magnificent ﴿in degrees, and greater in favoring﴾ than this world. Therefore one should devote oneself to it rather than to this world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 22:

﴿Forsaken﴾ — having no helper for you.

﴿Your Lord has decreed﴾ commanded ﴿that﴾ meaning, ﴿you worship none but Him﴾, and that you do good ﴿to your parents﴾ by being dutiful to them. ﴿If either or both of them reach old age with you﴾ is the subject (fa'il) of the verb; in another reading, ﴿يَبْلُغانِّ﴾ (yablughānni, in the dual), with ﴿أَحَدهما﴾ (aḥaduhumā) in apposition (badal) to the dual alif. ﴿Uff﴾ is pronounced with a fatḥa or a kasra on the fā', with or without tanwīn. It is a verbal noun meaning ﴿tabban وقُبْحًا﴾ (tabban wa qubḥan), that is, "perdition and ugliness." ﴿And do not rebuke them﴾ meaning, do not scold them. ﴿And speak to them a noble word﴾ meaning, a gentle and kind word.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 24:

﴿And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy﴾ — soften toward them your humble side ﴿out of mercy﴾, i.e., out of your tenderness toward them ﴿as﴾ they had mercy on me ﴿when they raised me when I was small﴾.

Your Lord knows best what is in your souls, [whether it is] concealing righteousness or disobedience, [so] if you are righteous, [that is, obedient to God], then indeed He is ever forgiving to those who turn back [in repentance, the ones who return] to His obedience, forgiving what has come from them against their parents in the way of a hasty lapse, while they do not harbour disobedience.
Give to the near of kin (dhu al-qurba) their due (haqqahu) of kindness and maintaining ties; and do not squander (tabdhir) wastefully, by spending in other than obedience to God.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 27:

﴿Indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils﴾, i.e., upon their way; ﴿and Satan is ever ungrateful to his Lord﴾, i.e., extremely disbelieving of His blessings; so too is the squanderer a brother of his.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 28:

﴿And if you turn away from them﴾, i.e., from those mentioned, the near of kin and those after them, and you do not give them, ﴿seeking mercy from your Lord, which you hope for﴾, i.e., in pursuit of a provision you await that will come to you, so that you may give them from it, ﴿then speak to them a gentle word﴾, soft and easy, by promising them the giving when the provision comes.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 29:

﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾, i.e., do not withhold it from spending altogether, ﴿nor extend it fully outstretched﴾ in spending, ﴿so that you sit blameworthy﴾, returning to the first [i.e., withholding], ﴿and destitute﴾, cut off, having nothing left with you, returning to the second [i.e., extravagance].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 30:

﴿Indeed, your Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it.﴾ He widens it (yuwassi'uhu) ﴿and restricts it﴾ He narrows it (yuḍayyiquhu) for whom He wills. ﴿Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾ knowing their inward and outward states, so He provides for them according to what is best for them (ʿalā ḥasab maṣāliḥihim).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 31:

﴿And do not kill your children⁠—﴾ by burying them alive (al-wa'd), ﴿out of fear of poverty⁠—﴾ fear of destitution, ﴿indeed, We provide for them and for you.⁠﴾ ﴿Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.⁠﴾ ﴿Great⁠—﴾ mighty.

﴿Do not approach﴾ is more emphatic than "do not commit" (لا تَأْتُوهُ). ﴿Immorality﴾ means something ugly (قَبِيحًا). ﴿And evil is﴾ means wretched (بِئْسَ), ﴿the way﴾ means a path (طَرِيقًا), ﴿it is﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 33:

﴿لِوَلِيِّهِ﴾ [to his heir (waliyyihi)] ﴿لِوارِثِهِ﴾ means to his heir; ﴿سُلْطانًا﴾ [authority (sultan)] means an authority (tasallut) over the killer; ﴿فَلا يُسْرِف﴾ [let him not exceed (yusrif)] means let him not go beyond the limit (yatajawaz al-hadd) ﴿فِي القَتْل﴾ [in killing (al-qatl)], by killing someone other than his killer, or by a means other than that with which he was killed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 34:

﴿And fulfil the covenant﴾ when you make a covenant with Allah or with people; ﴿for the covenant will be questioned﴾ it will be questioned about, i.e., the one who made it will be questioned about it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 35:

﴿And give full measure when you measure out, and weigh with a true balance.﴾ Complete the measure, ﴿with a true balance﴾, the upright scale. ﴿That is better and more favourable in outcome﴾, i.e., in its result (ma'al).

ولا تَقْفُ — "do not pursue" (tatba'): and al-fu'ad — the heart. ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all of these one will be questioned﴾. [Each of these] will be questioned about its owner: what he did with it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 37:**

﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾, i.e., arrogantly and with conceit. ﴿Indeed, you will never tear through the earth﴾, piercing it until you reach its end, ﴿by your arrogance﴾. ﴿And you will never reach the mountains in height﴾. The meaning is that you will not reach this extent, so how do you strut?
﴿All that﴾ the aforementioned

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 39:

﴿That is of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom﴾ O Muhammad, [i.e., the admonition (al-mawʿiẓa)], ﴿rejected﴾ expelled, banished from the mercy of God.

﴿Has He then chosen you for sons and taken for Himself daughters?﴾ *Asfākum* means *akhlaṣakum*, He purified you for Himself, O people of Makkah. ﴿Daughters﴾ means daughters for Himself, according to your claim. ﴿Indeed, you say﴾ means you say that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 41:

﴿And indeed We have diversified﴾ We made clear ﴿in this Qur'an﴾ of the parables, the promise and the warning ﴿that they may take heed﴾ that they may be admonished ﴿but it increases them in nothing﴾ that is, it does not increase them ﴿except aversion﴾ from the truth.
﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿If there were other gods with Him﴾, that is, Allah, ﴿they would have sought﴾, that is, sought ﴿a way to the Lord of the Throne﴾, that is, Allah, ﴿a path﴾, ﴿to fight Him﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 43:

﴿Subhanahu﴾ (Glorified is He), declaring Him far above ﴿and exalted above what they say﴾ of partners.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 44:

﴿Glorifying Him﴾ exalting Him (tunazzihuhu). ﴿And there is not a thing﴾ of the created beings ﴿but it glorifies [Him], [while] immersed in His praise﴾ (mutalabbisan bi-hamdihi), ﴿with His praise﴾, i.e., it says: "Subhan Allah wa bi-hamdihi" (Glory be to God and praise be to Him). ﴿But you do not understand﴾ you do not comprehend ﴿their glorification﴾, because it is not in your language. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾, in that He does not hasten to punish you.
﴿concealed﴾, meaning a veil concealing you from them so that they do not see you. It was revealed concerning those who intended to assassinate him (ﷺ).

﴿Akinnah﴾ (coverings) ﴿an yafqahūhu﴾ (that they understand it), i.e., from understanding the Qur'an; so they do not understand it. ﴿Wa fī ādhānihim waqran﴾ (and in their ears is a deafness), a heaviness, so they do not hear it. ﴿Nufūran﴾ (aversion), aversion from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 47:

﴿بِهِ﴾ (ﷺ, i.e., they listen to you) because of his [the Prophet's] mockery (bi-sababihi min al-huzu') ﴿إذْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إلَيْك﴾ ﴿when they listen to you﴾ to your recitation (ila qira'atika) ﴿وإذْ هُمْ نَجْوى﴾ ﴿and when they hold secret counsel﴾, conferring among themselves (yatanajawna baynahum), i.e., they talk together (ayy yatahaddathun) ﴿إذْ﴾ ﴿when﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the previous ﴿إذْ﴾ ﴿when﴾ ﴿يَقُول الظّالِمُونَ﴾ ﴿the wrongdoers say﴾ in their secret counsel ﴿إنْ﴾ ﴿you follow only﴾ ما ﴿a man bewitched﴾ مَسْحُورًا (makhdu'an, deceived; maghluban 'ala 'aqlihi, overcome in his reason)

Note on the translation: the passage as given is partly transliterated Arabic; I have rendered the Qur'anic words per the instructions, but the ﴿إنْ﴾ and ما elements are glossed as they appear in the source, and the Arabic phrases in parentheses are kept as transliterations.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 48:

﴿Look how they strike similitudes for you﴾ — calling you a man under sorcery, a soothsayer, and a poet — ﴿so they have gone astray﴾ by that from the guidance, ﴿and they cannot find a way﴾ a path leading to it.
﴿And they say﴾ denying the resurrection (al-ba'th)
﴿Say﴾ to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 51:

﴿Or a creation of what is greater in your breasts﴾ [i.e., something that is too great to accept life, let alone bones and dust, so the spirit must be made to come into being in you]. ﴿Then they will say, "Who will restore us"﴾ to life, ﴿Who created you﴾ [i.e., brought you into being] ﴿the first time﴾ when you were nothing? [The answer: the One who is able to originate is able to restore; indeed, restoration is easier.] ﴿Then they will shake their heads at you﴾ [i.e., move them] in amazement, ﴿and say﴾ mockingly, ﴿"When will it be?"﴾ [i.e., the Resurrection].

﴿On the day He calls you﴾: He will call out to you from the graves through the voice of Israfil. ﴿Then you will respond﴾: you will answer His call from the graves ﴿with His praise﴾: by His command. It is also said that it means ﴿with His praise﴾ in the sense that praise belongs to Him. ﴿You will think﴾ that ﴿you remained﴾ in the world ﴿but a little﴾, because of the terror of what you see.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 53:

﴿And say to My servants﴾ the believers, ﴿that they should say﴾ to the disbelievers the word ﴿that stirs up﴾ means corrupts ﴿Indeed, Satan is ever to man a clear enemy﴾ manifest in enmity; and the word which is better, and it is

Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy on you, by repentance and faith; or if He wills, He will punish you, by death in disbelief. We have not sent you as a guardian over them, to compel them to faith. This was before the command to fight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 55:

﴿And your Lord is most knowing of those in the heavens and the earth﴾, so He favours them with whatever He wills, according to their states. ﴿And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others﴾, by specifying each of them with a distinction, such as Musa with speech (kalam), Ibrahim with friendship (khullah), and Muhammad (ﷺ) with the Night Journey (isra').

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 56:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Call upon those you claimed﴾ to be gods ﴿besides Him﴾, such as the angels, Jesus and Uzayr (Ezra); ﴿they have no power to remove [the affliction]﴾ from you, ﴿nor to change it﴾ to anyone other than you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 57:

﴿Those whom they call upon﴾ — those whom they call upon as gods. ﴿seek﴾ — seek, desire. ﴿to their Lord the means of approach﴾ — nearness to Him through obedience. ﴿which of them﴾ — a substitute (badal) for the waw of yabtaghoon (they seek); meaning, it is the one who is ﴿nearest﴾ to Him who seeks it, so how much more so (is this true) of others. ﴿They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ — like the rest of them. So how can you call them gods?

﴿And there is not﴾ [the particle "ma" here is negative] ﴿a city﴾ [meaning its people are intended] ﴿but We will destroy it﴾ [through death] ﴿or punish it with a severe punishment﴾ [through killing and other means]. ﴿That was in the Book﴾ [al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet)] ﴿inscribed﴾ [written].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 59:

﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs﴾ which the people of Makkah proposed, ﴿except that the earlier peoples denied them﴾ when We sent them and We destroyed them. Had We sent them to these people, they would have denied them and deserved destruction. We have decreed to delay them so that the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) may be completed. ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel﴾ as a sign ﴿visible﴾, clear and evident, ﴿but they wronged themselves﴾ they disbelieved ﴿in it﴾ ﴿in the signs﴾, the miracles, ﴿and We send not the signs except as a warning﴾ to the servants, so that they may believe.

And remember, [O Muhammad], when We said to you: "Indeed your Lord encompasses the people" [with His knowledge and power, so they are within His grip. So convey [the message] to them, and do not fear anyone, for He will protect you from them]. "And We did not make the vision which We showed you" visibly, on the night of the Isra' (the Night Journey), "except as a trial for the people" of Makkah, when they denied it and some of them apostatized after he informed them of it. "And [We did not make] the accursed tree [mentioned] in the Qur'an" [a reference to al-Zaqqum, the tree that grows at the root of Hellfire]. "We made it a trial for them" when they said: "Fire burns trees, so how could it cause them to grow?" "And We warn them, but it increases them in nothing" [except greater rebellion, despite Our warning them with it].

﴿And﴾ mention [when] ﴿We said to the angels: "Prostrate to Adam"﴾, a prostration of greeting (*tahiyya*), performed by bowing, ﴿"from clay"﴾. The word *ṭīnan* (طِينًا) is in the accusative because the preposition has been dropped (*nazʿ al-khāfid*, removal of the governing preposition), so the sense is *min ṭīn* (مِن طِين), "from clay."

He said, "Have You considered this one whom You have honored above me? (i.e., tell me) Why did You favor him over me by commanding me to prostrate to him, when I am better than him: You created me from fire." ﴿If You give me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize (la-aḥtanikanna, "I will surely seize") and destroy his descendants by misguidance, except for a few of them whom You have protected.﴾

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 17, verse 63:

﴿He said﴾: the Most High said to him, ﴿Go﴾, being given respite until the time of the first blast. ﴿Your recompense﴾: you and they, ﴿a full recompense﴾: abundant, complete.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 64:

﴿And incite﴾ (istafziz) entice ﴿with your voice﴾ by your calling (people) to singing and musical instruments and every caller to disobedience; ﴿and urge on﴾ (wa-ajlib) shout ﴿against them with your cavalry and your infantry﴾, and they are the riders and the foot-soldiers in acts of disobedience; ﴿and share with them in wealth﴾ that is forbidden, such as usury (riba) and usurpation (ghasb), ﴿and in children﴾ born of fornication; ﴿and promise them﴾ that there will be no resurrection and no recompense; ﴿but Satan promises them nothing except delusion﴾, that is, falsehood.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 65:

﴿Indeed, My servants﴾ — the believers — ﴿you shall have no authority over them﴾ — no domination or power — ﴿and sufficient is your Lord as a Guardian﴾ — a Protector for them from you.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 17, verse 66:

﴿يُزْجِي﴾ (Yuzjī) means yajrī (causes to run/sail). ﴿لَكُمْ الفُلْك﴾ (for you the ships) means the al-sufun (ships). ﴿لِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ (that you may seek) means tatlubū (you seek). ﴿مِن فَضْله﴾ (of His bounty) means Exalted is He, through trade. ﴿إنّهُ كانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا﴾ (Indeed He has ever been Merciful to you) refers to His subjecting them to you (i.e., making the ships subservient for you).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 67:

﴿The harm⁠﴾ the hardship ﴿at sea﴾ the fear of drowning ﴿has strayed⁠﴾ has been lost to you ﴿those whom you invoke⁠﴾ whom you worship of the gods, so you do not invoke them ﴿except Him⁠﴾ the Exalted, for you invoke Him alone, because you are in a hardship that none removes except Him ﴿Then when He delivers you⁠﴾ from drowning and brings you safely to land ﴿you turn away⁠﴾ from monotheism ﴿and man is ever ungrateful⁠﴾ denying the favours.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: "Land's side" means: the earth, like Qarun. "Or He sends against you a sandstorm": that is, He pelts you with pebbles, like the people of Lot. "Then you will find no guardian" against Him: no protector from Him.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 17, verse 69:

﴿Therein﴾, i.e., in the sea, ﴿at another time﴾, once, ﴿a violent wind﴾, i.e., a fierce wind that does not pass by anything without shattering it, so that it breaks your ships, ﴿and then drowns you for your disbelief﴾, because of your kufr, ﴿and you will find no avenger﴾ (tabi'an), i.e., no helper and no follower who will demand from Us [retribution] for what We did to you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 70:

﴿And We have certainly honoured﴾ — ﴿fadalna﴾ (We favoured) — ﴿the children of Adam﴾ — with knowledge, speech, the balance of their creation, and other things, among which is their purity after death. ﴿And We carried them﴾ — upon beasts — ﴿on the land and the sea﴾ — upon ships — ﴿and provided for them of the good things﴾ — ﴿and [We] preferred them over much of what We created﴾ — such as the cattle and the wild beasts — ﴿with a [clear] preference﴾. Here "man" (man) is in the sense of "mā" (what), or it retains its own usage, and it includes the angels. The intended meaning is the preference of the species, and it does not necessitate the preference of every individual, since they (the angels) are superior to humankind other than the Prophets.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 71:

﴿with their Imam﴾ (i.e., their Prophet); it will be said, "O community of so-and-so," or [it will be said] with their book of deeds, and it will be said, "O companion of evil," and that is on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then whoever is given﴾ among them ﴿his book in his right hand﴾, and they are the felicitous, the people of insight in the world, ﴿they will not be wronged﴾ (yunqasūn: they will not have any of their deeds diminished) ﴿a fatil﴾ (the measure of the thin skin of a date stone).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 72:

﴿And whoever was blind in this [world]﴾, i.e., in this world, to the truth, ﴿will be blind in the Hereafter﴾, regarding the path of salvation and the recitation of the Qur'an, ﴿and more astray in way﴾, further away from it in path. It was revealed concerning Thaqif when they asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to make their valley sacred, and they persisted in this demand upon him.

﴿And if﴾ is *mukhaffafa* (the lightened form of *inna*), ﴿they were almost﴾ (*kadu*: came close to) ﴿tempting you﴾ (*layastanzilunaka*: to make you slip down, to lure you away) ﴿and then﴾ (*wa-idhan*: in that case) [it would be so] if you had done that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 74:

﴿And had We not made you firm﴾ upon the truth through protection (ʿiṣmah) ﴿you would almost have inclined﴾ meaning, you would have come close to leaning ﴿toward them a little﴾ meaning, inclining ﴿a little﴾ because of the intensity of their scheming and their insistence; and this is explicit that he (ﷺ) neither inclined nor came close.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 17, verse 75:

﴿Then﴾ (i.e., if you had inclined) ﴿double the life﴾, i.e., double the punishment, ﴿and double the death﴾, i.e., twice what others are punished with in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿you would not have found any helper against Us﴾, i.e., any preventer from it.

It was revealed when the Jews said to him: "If you are a prophet, then go to al-Sham (Syria), for it is the land of the prophets." ﴿And if﴾ (the particle "in" here is light, i.e. mukhaffafah) ﴿they had almost driven you out of the land﴾, meaning the land of Madinah, ﴿then they would not have remained after you﴾ (khilafak, i.e. after you) therein ﴿except for a little while﴾, then they would have been destroyed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 77:

﴿Such has been Our way with the messengers We sent before you﴾ i.e., like Our practice with them, by destroying those who expelled them, ﴿and you will not find any change in Our way﴾ tahwilan (تَحْوِيلًا) meaning substitution, alteration.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 78:

﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾, i.e., from the time of its decline (zawal), ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾, i.e., the coming of its darkness: that is, the noon (zuhr), afternoon (asr), sunset (maghrib) and night (isha) prayers. ﴿And the recitation of dawn﴾, i.e., the dawn prayer (salat al-subh). ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾, witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

﴿So keep vigil⁠﴾ (fa-tahajjad), i.e., pray (fa-salli) ﴿with it⁠﴾ (bihi), with the Qur'an, ﴿as a supererogatory prayer for you⁠﴾ (nafilatan laka), i.e., an additional obligation specific to you, not to your community; or it is a virtue over the obligatory prayers. ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you⁠﴾ (yab'athaka), i.e., establish you, ﴿to a praised station⁠﴾ (maqaman mahmudan) in the Hereafter, in which the first and the last will praise you. It is the station of intercession (al-shafa'ah) in the judgment of the decision (fi fasl al-qada'). It was revealed when he was commanded to emigrate (al-hijrah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 80:

﴿Admit me﴾ into the city (al-Madinah) ﴿with a truthful admission﴾, an admission that is pleasing, in which I see nothing I dislike. ﴿And bring me out﴾ of Makkah ﴿with a truthful exit﴾, an exit in which I do not turn my heart back toward it. ﴿And grant me from Yourself an authority, a helper﴾, a power by which You support me against Your enemies.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 81:

﴿And say﴾ upon your entering Makkah, ﴿"The truth has come"﴾ (i.e., Islam), ﴿and falsehood has vanished﴾ (i.e., disbelief has perished). ﴿Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish﴾ (mudmahillan, i.e., perishing and passing away).

"He (ﷺ) entered it while there were three hundred and sixty idols around the House, and he began striking them with a stick in his hand and saying this, until they fell." Narrated by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 82:

﴿And We send down﴾ [of the Qur'an] for clarification, ﴿a healing﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and a mercy for the believers﴾ in it, ﴿but it does not increase the wrongdoers﴾ who are disbelievers ﴿except in loss﴾ because of their disbelief in it.

﴿The human being﴾, the disbeliever, ﴿turns away﴾ from gratitude, ﴿and turns aside [with] his side﴾, bending his side in arrogance. ﴿And when evil touches him﴾, meaning poverty and hardship, ﴿he is despairing﴾, despondent of God's mercy.
﴿Say: Each﴾ [of us], from us and from you, ﴿acts according to his shakilah﴾ [i.e., his manner, his way], ﴿who is better guided as to the way﴾ [i.e., as to a way], so He will reward him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 85:

﴿They ask you﴾, i.e., the Jews, ﴿about the spirit﴾, which is that by which the body is given life. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿The spirit is of the affair of my Lord﴾, i.e., it is of His knowledge, which you do not know. ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾, in comparison with His knowledge, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 86:

﴿Wa-la-in﴾ the lam is a lam of oath (lam al-qasam). ﴿We have revealed to you﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿that We could take it away﴾ by erasing it from the breasts and the codices (al-masahif).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 87:

﴿Illa﴾ (except) — but We have preserved it, ﴿as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His bounty toward you has been great﴾ — great, magnificent — in that He sent it down to you and gave you the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud) and other virtues.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (*Tafsir al-Jalalayn*, a concise commentary by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti) on surah 17, verse 88:

﴿Like this Qur'an﴾ in eloquence and rhetoric, ﴿ظَهِيرًا﴾ (zahīran, meaning "a helper"), giving aid. It was revealed in response to their saying: ﴿And if We willed, we would say the like of this﴾.

And We have certainly diversified (explained clearly) for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, that they might take heed. ...

**Translation:**

﴿And We have certainly explained﴾ (clarified) ﴿every example﴾ — an attributive adjective of an omitted noun, meaning: an example of the kind of every example, ﴿so that they might take heed﴾. ﴿But most of the people﴾ — that is, the people of Makkah — ﴿refused except disbelief﴾, denial of the truth.
﴿And they said﴾ is coordinated (ʿaṭf, grammatical conjunction) with أبى (abā, "refused") [in the preceding verse]. ﴿A spring﴾ means a spring (ʿayn) from which water gushes, عينا ينبع منها الماء.
﴿A garden﴾ an orchard, ﴿within it﴾ its midst.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 92:

﴿Kisafan﴾ (pieces) ﴿qabilan﴾ (face to face, and openly, so that we see them)

﴿Zukhruf﴾ (gold) ﴿or ascend﴾ (climb) ﴿into the sky﴾ by means of a ladder. ﴿And we will not believe in your ascent﴾ even if you ascended into it ﴿until you bring down upon us﴾ from it ﴿a Book﴾ containing confirmation of you. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Glory be to my Lord!﴾ (an expression of wonder). ﴿Am I﴾ (here "هَلْ" means "مَا", i.e. "I am not") ﴿anything but a human messenger﴾ like the other messengers? They did not bring a sign except by the permission of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 94:

﴿Except that they said﴾ i.e., their saying, in denial: ﴿Has God sent a human being as a messenger?﴾ and He did not send an angel.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 95:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿If there were angels walking calmly on the earth﴾ instead of humans, ﴿We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger﴾, since a messenger is sent to a people only from their own kind, so that they can address him and understand from him.
"Sufficient as a witness between me and you" — as a witness to my truthfulness, "Knowing and Seeing" — knowing their inner states and their outward conditions.

"So you will not find for them any protectors who could guide them, and We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection, walking (on their faces), their refuge will be Hell; whenever its flame subsides, We will increase them in blaze" — that is, its flame will be kindled and intensified.

Note on the wording: the text reads "﴿فَلَنْ تَجِد لَهُمْ أوْلِياء﴾" which I have rendered as in the Qur'anic quotation above, and the gloss "يَهْدُونَهُمْ" as "who could guide them."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 98:

﴿That is because they disbelieved in Our signs and said﴾ denying the resurrection, ﴿"When we are bones and crumbled dust, shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?"﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 99:

﴿Do they not see﴾ i.e., do they not know ﴿that God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ despite their greatness ﴿is able to create the likes of them﴾ i.e., humans, in their smallness ﴿and He has appointed for them a term﴾ for death and resurrection ﴿but the wrongdoers refuse except to deny﴾ denial of it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 100:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord﴾, of provision and rain, ﴿then you would withhold﴾, you would be stingy, ﴿for fear of spending﴾, for fear that they would be exhausted by spending, so that you would be frugal, ﴿being niggardly﴾, stingy.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 101:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs.﴾ They are: the hand, the staff, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, or the obliteration [of the Pharaoh's people], and the reduction of fruits. ﴿So ask﴾ O Muhammad ﴿the Children of Israel﴾ about it, a question meant to confirm to the polytheists the truth of your claim; or [it means] We said to him: "Ask." And in one reading it is in the past tense (fa-sa'ala). ﴿[Moses], bewitched﴾, deceived, overpowered in your intellect.

﴿He said: "You certainly know that none has sent down these (the verses)†except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear proofs."﴾ Clear proofs: lessons (ʿibar). "But you are obstinate." In another recitation (qirāʾah), the tā' is read with a ḍammah, as عَلِمْتُ (ʿalimtu), meaning "I know." ﴿And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed.﴾ Doomed: destroyed, or turned away from good.

† The commentary's word here is "al-āyāt," which glosses the pronoun "these."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 103:

﴿So he intended﴾ Pharaoh ﴿to drive them﴾ out, i.e., to expel Musa and his people ﴿from the land﴾, the land of Egypt.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 104:

﴿When the promise of the Hereafter comes﴾, i.e., the Hour, ﴿We will bring you all together in a mass﴾, all of you, you and them together.

And with the truth We have sent it down, and with the truth it has descended. (Surah 17, verse 105) ﴿And with the truth We have sent it down﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿and with the truth﴾ that it contains, ﴿it descended﴾ just as it was sent down, untouched by any alteration. ﴿And We have not sent you, O Muhammad, except as a bringer of good news﴾ to whoever believes in Paradise, ﴿and a warner﴾ to whoever disbelieves in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 106:

﴿And a Qur'an﴾ is in the accusative, governed by a verb implied by ﴿We divided it﴾ (farraqnāhu), which it explains: We sent it down in portions over twenty or twenty-three years. ﴿In order that you may recite it at leisure﴾ (mukth): gently and deliberately, so that they may understand it. ﴿And We sent it down, a gradual sending down﴾ (tanzīlan): piece by piece, according to what the interests require.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 107:

﴿Say﴾ to the disbelievers of Makkah: ﴿Believe in it or do not believe﴾ — a threat to them. ﴿Before it﴾, i.e., before its revelation, ﴿those who were given knowledge﴾ — and they are the believers among the People of the Book.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 17, verse 108:

﴿And they say, "Glory be to our Lord"﴾, exalting Him above breaking His promise. ﴿إنْ﴾ is a lightened form (mukhaffafah, the lightened form of inna), and ﴿the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled﴾, by its descent and by the sending of the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿And they fall down upon their chins, weeping﴾ — a conjunction (ʿaṭf) with the addition of an attribute. ﴿And it increases them in humility (khushūʿan)﴾ — the Qur'an increases them in humility (tawāḍuʿan) before Allah.

Al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 17, verse 110:

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, O Most Merciful." They said: "He forbids us to worship two gods, yet he calls upon another god along with Him." So there was revealed: ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: name Him by either of them, or call upon Him by saying: "O Allah, O Most Merciful." ﴿Whichever﴾ "أيًّا" is conditional (شَرْطِيَّة, *shartiyyah*), and "ما" is superfluous (زائِدَة, *za'idah*), meaning: whichever of these two names ﴿you call﴾ upon, ﴿He has the most beautiful names﴾ "فَلَهُ الأَسْماء الحُسْنى," meaning: for the one named by them. ﴿These two are among them.﴾ This is what is indicated by the hadith: "Allah, there is no god but Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, the King, the Holy, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Supreme, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, the Oft-Forgiving, the Subduer, the Giver, the Provider, the Opener, the All-Knowing, the Restrainer, the Expander, the Abaser, the Exalter, the Bestower of Honour, the Humiliator, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Judge, the Just, the Subtle, the All-Aware, the Forbearing, the Magnificent, the Forgiving, the Appreciative, the Most High, the Great, the Preserver, the Nourisher, the Reckoner, the Majestic, the Generous, the Watchful, the Responsive, the Vast, the Wise, the Loving, the Glorious, the Raiser, the Witness, the Truth, the Trustee, the Strong, the Firm, the Protector, the Praiseworthy, the Counter, the Originator, the Restorer, the Giver of Life, the Causer of Death, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Finder, the Glorious, the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, the Capable, the Powerful, the Expediter, the Delayer, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Governor, the Exalted, the Benevolent, the Relenting, the Avenger, the Pardoner, the Compassionate, the Master of the Kingdom, Possessor of Majesty and Honour, the Equitable, the Gatherer, the Self-Sufficient, the Enricher, the Preventer, the Harmer, the Benefactor, the Light, the Guide, the Incomparable, the Everlasting, the Inheritor, the Guide to Right Conduct, the Patient." Related by al-Tirmidhi.

﴿Do not recite your prayer aloud﴾, meaning: do not recite it loudly, lest the polytheists hear you and revile you, and revile the Qur'an and the One who revealed it. ﴿Nor recite it in a low voice﴾, meaning: do not recite it so quietly ﴿that﴾ your companions cannot benefit from it. ﴿And seek﴾, meaning: aim for, ﴿between these two﴾, meaning: loudness and inaudibility, ﴿a way﴾, meaning: a middle path.

﴿a partner in the dominion﴾ in divinity. ﴿And He has no protector﴾ who helps Him ﴿out of﴾ humiliation, meaning He is not humbled so as to need a helper. ﴿And magnify Him with full magnification﴾: exalt Him with complete exaltation, above taking a son, having a partner, being humbled, and everything that does not befit Him. The ordering of praise upon this is to indicate that He alone deserves all praise, for the perfection of His essence and the uniqueness of His attributes. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad (a collection of hadiths arranged by narrator) from Mu'adh al-Juhani, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he used to say: ﴿The verse of might: All praise is due to Allah, who has not taken a son and has had no partner in the dominion﴾, to the end of the surah. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

The author said: This is the end of what I completed of the tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) of the Noble Qur'an, which was composed by the Shaykh, the Imam, the scholar, the verifier Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him. I have devoted myself to completing it, and in the ambiguous verses reliance and dependence are upon it. May Allah have mercy on a man who looks at it with an eye of fairness, and comes upon an error in it, and informs me of it. I have said: I praise Allah, my Lord, that He guided me to what I have produced despite my incapacity and weakness. Who am I to be free from error so that it may be corrected? And who am I to be accepted, even with a single letter of this? It had never been in my mind to undertake this, knowing my inability to delve into these paths. Perhaps Allah will benefit by it greatly and open with it hearts that are sealed, and eyes and ears that are deaf. I think of one who is accustomed to lengthy works, who has turned away from this completion and its origin entirely, and has turned to open obstinacy, and has not directed his understanding to its subtleties: ﴿And whoever is blind in this world, he will be blind in the Hereafter﴾. May Allah grant us through it guidance to the path of truth, success, and insight into the subtleties and verifications of His words, and make us through it ﴿among those whom Allah has blessed: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous; and excellent companions they are﴾.

He finished its composition on Sunday, the tenth of Shawwal, in the year 870 AH. The beginning was on Wednesday, the first of Ramadan of the aforementioned year. He finished its whitening (final clean copy) on Wednesday, the sixth of Safar, in the year 871 AH. And Allah knows best.

Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Khatib al-Tukhi said: My friend, the scholar Kamal al-Din al-Mahalli, brother of our shaykh Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli, may Allah have mercy on them both, informed me that he saw his brother, the aforementioned Jalal al-Din, in a dream, and before him was our friend, the scholar and verifier Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti, the author of this completion. The shaykh had taken this completion in his hand and was leafing through it, and he said to its aforementioned author: "Which is better, my arrangement or yours?" He said: "Mine." He said: "Look," and he presented to him places in it, as if gently pointing to objections in them. Whenever he raised something to him, the author of this completion would answer it, while the shaykh smiled and laughed.

Our shaykh, the Imam, the scholar Jalal al-Din Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Suyuti, author of this completion, said: What I believe and affirm is that the arrangement which the shaykh Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli, may Allah have mercy on him, set down in his portion is better than my arrangement by many levels. How could it not be, when most of what I have set down here is borrowed from his arrangement and derived from it? I have no doubt about that. As for what was seen in the dream written above, perhaps the shaykh pointed by it to the few places where I departed from his arrangement for a particular reason. These are very few, I think they do not reach ten places. Among them: the shaykh said in Surah Sad: "The spirit is a subtle body by which a person lives through its penetration into him." I had followed him initially, and I mentioned this definition in Surah al-Hijr, then I struck it out, because of the verse ﴿And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord﴾, which is explicit, or nearly explicit, that the spirit is of the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, which we do not know. So refraining from defining it is better. For this reason the shaykh Taj al-Din ibn al-Subki said in Jam' al-Jawami': "Muhammad (ﷺ) did not speak about the spirit, so we refrain from it." Among them: the shaykh said in Surah al-Hajj: "The Sabians are a sect of the Jews." I mentioned this in Surah al-Baqarah and added "or the Christians" as an explanation of a second opinion, for it is the well-known one, especially among our jurist companions. In al-Minhaj: "Although the Samaritans differ from the Jews, and the Sabians from the Christians in their fundamental religion." In its commentary: al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, explicitly stated that the Sabians are a sect of the Christians. I cannot now recall a third place. So it seems the shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, is pointing to something like this. And Allah knows best what is correct, and to Him is the return and the final resort.
